question.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t}-1\,,{e}^{-2t}\,⟩$ at the point $P(0,1),$ valid for all real values of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
The point $P(0,1)$  is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$ At this point,  the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
R(u)=r({t}_{0})+u\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,\,1⟩ \\ ⟨{e}^{t}-1\,,{e}^{-2t}⟩ & =⟨0,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the components yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}-1=0 \\ {e}^{-2t}=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the first equation, we get $t=0.$ This value also satisfies the other equation. Therefore,  $P(0,1)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(0).$

We calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}-1)\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-2t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-2{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point  $P(0,1)$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨0\,,\,1⟩+u⟨1\,,\,-2⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
